1. Petroleum and chemical Tankers Business (PCT)
oQ4/2025, revenue and GP slightly declined from 
Q3/2025 due mainly to the monsoon and 
subsequent severe flood in southern Thailand, 
which led to lower consumption of refined oil 
and tensions along the Thailand –Cambodia 
border.
oDuring suspension of oil shipments routing to 
Cambodia in Q4/2025, the available tankers 
were rerouted to serve other international 
markets to mitigate financial impact from the 
suspension. As a result, FY2025 GP declined only 
11%.
oPRM is planning to continue pursuing more 
international customers as quality of our vessels 
and services are well recognized by international 
markets.

3. Floating Storage Unit Business (FSU)
oFSU’s business benefited from increased storage 
demand and a higher charter rate in 2025.
oThe benefit was partially offset by unusually 
strong Thai Baht throughout the year.
oAs a result, FY2025 revenue and GP marginally 
declined from FY2024, despite the replacement 
FSU (replacing one sold at Q1/2025), which was 
not available until May 2025.
oQ4/2025 GP declined 9% from Q4/2024 due to 
the higher depreciated cost of the new FSU VS 
the old one, which was fully depreciated at the 
end of 2023. However, the new FSU will be more 
attractive to customers due to its newer age and 
better condition.
oQ4/2025 revenue and GP dropped from 
Q3/2025 due to one month off -hiring of 2 FSUs for 
cargo rearrangements to allow more available 
cargo space in one vessel for key customer.
*The 5th FSU vessel commence operation in May 2025

➢ 2020: Global oil demand contracted sharply due to worldwide lockdown 
measures and the near -cessation of travel and aviation. 
➢ 2022–2023:  Global oil consumption exceeded its 2019 level, despite 
heightened price volatility from the war and OPEC+ production cut policy, 
as oil use continued to expand alongside the full reopening of economies 
after COVID and the rebound in tourism and aviation worldwide. 
➢ 2024–2026: Global oil demand is expected to continue growing, however at 
a slower pace than during the post -COVID rebound. However, non -OECD 
economies, particularly in Asia are likely to see steady growth, supported 
by rising household incomes, urban expansion, and faster growth in 
industry and petrochemicals relative to other regions.
Thailand Oil Consumption: 
➢ Jet A -1: Domestic Jet A -1 consumption fell sharply in 2020 due to lockdown 
measures. Since 2021, consumption has been recovering steadily but 
remains below pre -COVID levels.
➢ Diesel: Domestic diesel consumption remains elevated, with the usual 
seasonal volatility.
➢ Gasoline (motor gasoline): Gasoline consumption is broadly unchanged 
compared with the pre -COVID period, despite Thailand’s relatively rapid 
adoption of electric vehicles (EVs).

16Company Statement on Fake New in the Media 
With reference to images and information posted on 
the X platform alleging that an oil tanker named 
“Prima” was attacked by drones in the Strait of 
Hormuz and which used a photograph of “Sri Phuket,” 
a vessel owned by Prima Marine Public Company 
Limited (PRM) the Company hereby issues the 
following clarification to prevent any public 
misunderstanding:
Vessel Identification
The Company does not own or operate any vessel 
named “Prima,” as alleged. 
Trading Route
Sri Phuket is a domestic oil -transport vessel operating 
exclusively within Thai waters. The vessel does not 
trade to the Middle East and has not sailed in or near 
the Strait of Hormuz, contrary to the claims in the 
posts.
Safety of Assets and Personnel
The Company confirms that Sri Phuket and all crew 
members are operating normally and safely. The 
Company has no involvement whatsoever with the 
conflict or war -related incidents referenced in the 
aforementioned posts.
